---
title: "1.1.4. Graph Diffusion via the System of SDEs (GDSS)"
bibliography: ../../references.bib
---

Following the [Stochastic Differential Equations (SDEs)](sde.qmd) connection with generative diffusion, Graph Diffusion via the System of SDEs (GDSS) [@dm:gdss] extended this approach to graph generation. The idea was to couple the diffusion of the adjacency and node features, creating a system of SDEs.

Let $\boldsymbol G = (\boldsymbol X, \boldsymbol A) \in \mathbb R^{N\times d} \times \mathbb R^{N\times N}$ be a graph composed of a weighted adjacency matrix $\boldsymbol A$ and $N$ node features $\boldsymbol X$ of dimension $d$. To jointly diffuse the nodes and edges, the diffusion process is formulated by building a trajectory $\{\boldsymbol G_t = (\boldsymbol X_t, \boldsymbol A_t)\}_{t\in [0, T]}$, where $T$ is the end of the diffusion process. For that, each component of the graph is corrupted independently, following: 
$$
\begin{cases}
d\boldsymbol{X} = \boldsymbol{f}_{\boldsymbol{X}}(\boldsymbol{X}, t) dt + g_{\boldsymbol{X}}(t)  d\boldsymbol{w}_{\boldsymbol{X}} \\
d\boldsymbol{A} = \boldsymbol{f}_{\boldsymbol{A}}(\boldsymbol{A}, t) dt + g_{\boldsymbol{A}}(t)  d\boldsymbol{w}_{\boldsymbol{A}}
\end{cases},
$$ {#eq-1}
where $\boldsymbol f(\boldsymbol G, t) = (\boldsymbol f_{\boldsymbol X} (\boldsymbol X), \boldsymbol f_{\boldsymbol A} (\boldsymbol A))$ are the drift components, $g_{\boldsymbol X}$ and $g_{\boldsymbol A}$ are the diffusion coefficients, and $\boldsymbol{\overline{w}_{\boldsymbol X}}$ and $\boldsymbol{\overline{w}_{\boldsymbol A}}$ are the respective Wiener processes running backwards in time. That enabled each component to have its own corruption parameters. Although the forward processes are independent, the reverse process is jointly coupled, due to the direct relation between nodes and links. The problem is that the joint score function belongs to a heterogeneous space, composed of the space of nodes and the space of the links. To overcome this issue, a system of reverse time SDEs was proposed, following:
$$
\begin{cases}
d\boldsymbol X = \left[\boldsymbol f_{\boldsymbol X}(\boldsymbol X, t) - g_{\boldsymbol X}(t)^2 \nabla_{\boldsymbol X} \log p_t(\boldsymbol X, \boldsymbol A) \right] dt + g_{\boldsymbol X}(t) \boldsymbol{\overline{w}_{\boldsymbol X}} \\
d\boldsymbol A = \left[\boldsymbol f_{\boldsymbol A}(\boldsymbol A, t) - g_{\boldsymbol A}(t)^2 \nabla_{\boldsymbol A} \log p_t(\boldsymbol X, \boldsymbol A) \right] dt + g_{\boldsymbol A}(t) \boldsymbol{\overline{w}_{\boldsymbol A}}
\end{cases},
$$ {#eq-2}
With that, each graph component was diffused separately, while their reverse time SDEs were coupled by the joint score function of the data distribution.

To approximate these partial score functions, GDSS employed Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) parameterized by $\boldsymbol{\theta}$ and $\boldsymbol \phi$. The GNNs received the noisy graph tuple $(\boldsymbol{X}_t, \boldsymbol{A}_t)$ at time $t$, respectively approximating one of the partial score functions:
$$
\boldsymbol{s}_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}(\boldsymbol{X}_t, \boldsymbol{A}_t, t) \approx \nabla_{\boldsymbol{X}} \log p_t(\boldsymbol{X}, \boldsymbol{A}) \quad \text{and} \quad \boldsymbol{s}_{\boldsymbol{\phi}}(\boldsymbol{X}_t, \boldsymbol{A}_t, t) \approx \nabla_{\boldsymbol{A}} \log p_t(\boldsymbol{X}, \boldsymbol{A}).
$$ {#eq-4}
By sharing the topological structure as input, the estimation of the node and edge scores remained coupled, even though the networks $\boldsymbol{\theta}$ and $\boldsymbol{\phi}$ were optimized independently.

The models were trained using a joint denoising score matching objective, which minimized:
$$
\mathcal{L}(\boldsymbol{\theta}, \boldsymbol{\phi}) = \mathbb{E}_{t, \boldsymbol{G}_0, \boldsymbol{G}_t} \left[  \mathcal L(\boldsymbol \theta) + \mathcal L(\boldsymbol \phi) \right],
$$ {#eq-5}
where:
$$
\mathcal L(\boldsymbol \theta) = \lambda_{\boldsymbol{X}}(t) \left\| \boldsymbol{s}_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}(\boldsymbol{X}_t, \boldsymbol{A}_t, t) - \nabla_{\boldsymbol{X}_t} \log q_{0t}(\boldsymbol{X}_t \mid \boldsymbol{X}_0) \right\|_2^2,
$$ {#eq-6}
$$
\mathcal L(\boldsymbol \phi) = \lambda_{\boldsymbol{A}}(t) \left\| \boldsymbol{s}_{\boldsymbol{\phi}}(\boldsymbol{X}_t, \boldsymbol{A}_t, t) - \nabla_{\boldsymbol{A}_t} \log q_{0t}(\boldsymbol{A}_t \mid \boldsymbol{A}_0) \right\|_2^2,
$$ {#eq-7}
and $q_{0t}$ represents the perturbation kernel of the forward SDEs, with $\lambda_{\boldsymbol{X}} : \mathbb R \to \mathbb R$ and $\lambda_{\boldsymbol{A}} : \mathbb R \to \mathbb R$ being positive weighting functions. Here, $t\sim \mathcal U(0, T)$, $\boldsymbol G_0 \sim p_0(\boldsymbol G)$ and $\boldsymbol G_t \sim p_t(\boldsymbol{G})$.

In order to sample from the model, a two-step procedure was employed. First, the size of the graph was sampled from the empirical distribution of graph sizes in the training data. Given $N$, algorithms based on [Predictor-Corrector (PC)](../samplers/sde_samplers.qmd) were developed to sample from the system of revere time SDEs.
